item.title: Yankees, White Sox and Padres sweep into division series
item.description: Three wild-card series ended in two-game sweeps. The Yankees routed Boston 9-2, the White Sox beat Houston 7-3 for their first postseason series victory since 2005, and the Padres topped the Cubs 4-1. Philadelphia forced a decisive Game 3 with a 10-inning win over Atlanta.

item.title: Senate sends sweeping college-sports bill to the House
item.description: The Senate passed the Protect College Sports Act 77-22, proposing national rules for athlete compensation and transfers, new scholarship and health protections, and limited antitrust protection for the NCAA. The measure faces an uncertain path in a House that is out until after the midterm elections.

item.title: NFL tells Rams a decisive pass-interference flag was wrong
item.description: Sean McVay said the NFL acknowledged that Rams cornerback Josh Wallace should not have been flagged late against Denver. The penalty erased an interception and gave the Broncos a first down; Bo Nix scored the winning touchdown six plays later. The admission sharpens the perennial debate over reviewable judgment calls.

item.title: MLB wild-card openers deliver three routs and a Braves comeback
item.description: Austin Riley's three-run homer in the eighth lifted Atlanta over Philadelphia 5-3 in the wild-card opener. The Yankees blanked Boston 9-0 behind Cam Schlittler and Ben Rice, San Diego shut out the Cubs 8-0, and the White Sox beat Houston 6-3 for their first postseason win since the 2005 World Series.

item.title: Liberty become first No. 8 seed to oust WNBA's No. 1
item.description: New York swept top-seeded Minnesota with an 87-71 win, becoming the first No. 8 seed to eliminate a No. 1 in the WNBA's 30-year history. Jonquel Jones had 21 points and 13 rebounds, Breanna Stewart scored 21, and Sabrina Ionescu added 18 as the Liberty advanced to the semifinals.

item.title: U.S. captain Tim Ream retires from international soccer
item.description: Tim Ream retired from the U.S. national team at 38 after 86 appearances across 16 years. The Charlotte FC defender won two CONCACAF Nations League titles and captained the Americans at this summer's World Cup, where they reached the round of 16 before losing to Belgium.

item.title: Case Keenum leads Bears past Eagles in surprise start
item.description: Case Keenum, making his first NFL appearance since December 2023, threw for 247 yards and two touchdowns and ran for another score as Chicago routed Philadelphia 27-7. The 38-year-old third-stringer completed 24 of 34 passes, while the Bears' defense forced three turnovers.

item.title: Baseball labor standoff raises lockout risk
item.description: Major League Baseball's labor standoff is moving toward a possible lockout after the collective bargaining agreement expires Dec. 1. Players say they will fight a salary cap, while owners argue the game's economics need repair—putting spring training and even Opening Day at risk.

item.title: Djokovic returns to unbeaten Beijing ground
item.description: Novak Djokovic returns at the China Open for his first match since a U.S. Open semifinal exit. The 39-year-old says his body feels good, carries a 29-0 Beijing record with six titles, and is still chasing a record 25th major championship.

item.title: U.S. completes record Presidents Cup comeback
item.description: In a major reversal from Saturday's three-point deficit, the United States won nine of 12 Sunday singles and halved the last match to beat the International team 17-13. The biggest singles-day rout in Presidents Cup history extended the Americans' winning streak to 11.

item.title: Ravens beat Cowboys on seven-second drive in Rio
item.description: Baltimore needed only seven seconds to steal a 34-31 win in the NFL's first regular-season game in Rio. Lamar Jackson hit Zay Flowers for 27 yards, the Ravens called timeout with one second left, and Tyler Loop made a 56-yard field goal.

item.title: Astros take AL West with an 81-81 record
item.description: Houston routed the Athletics 9-0 to win its fifth AL West title in six years despite finishing 81-81. The Astros became the first division champion in major-league history without a winning record, an odd final twist to baseball's expanded-playoff era.

item.title: Justin Verlander closes 21-year career with a family moment
item.description: Justin Verlander finished what he says will be his final major-league start, then watched 7-year-old daughter Genevieve sprint to the mound for a hug. The 43-year-old, a three-time Cy Young winner and 2017 World Series champion, walked off hand-in-hand with her after 21 seasons.

item.title: No. 21 Florida knocks off No. 4 Ole Miss, 52-28
item.description: Jadan Baugh powered Florida's 52-28 upset of fourth-ranked Ole Miss as the Gators turned a marquee SEC matchup into a statement win. Florida's ground game repeatedly broke through a defense that entered the weekend with national-title ambitions, reshaping the early conference race.

item.title: U.S. trims Presidents Cup deficit, trails by three entering singles
item.description: A day after the International side swept Friday foursomes, the U.S. answered on Saturday and cut the Presidents Cup margin to 10½-7½. That significant shift leaves the Americans within three points before Sunday's 12 singles matches at Medinah, keeping a comeback—and the International team's bid to end a long drought—alive.
